(अम्), n. a sin offering; (ई), f. a species of tree; [cf. शमी।] —पाप-शील, अस्, आ, अम्, ill-disposed, prone to evil, of bad character, wicked. —पाप-शोधन, अस्, आ, अम्, cleansing or washing away sins; (अम्), n., N. of a Tīrtha. —पाप-संशमन, अस्, आ, अम्, removing sin. —पाप-सङ्कल्प, अस्, आ, अम्, evil-minded, ill-intentioned. —पाप-सम, अम्, n., Ved. a bad year. —पाप-सम्मित, अस्, आ, अम्, equal in sin, of like guilt. —पाप-सूदन, अस्, आ, अम्, sin-destroying. —पापसूदन-तीर्थ, अम्, n., N. of a Tīrtha. —पाप-हन्, आ, घ्नी, अ, sin-destroying, destroying the wicked. —पाप-हर, अस्, आ, अम्, removing evil, destroying sin; (अम्), n. a means of removing evil; (आ), f., N. of a river. —पापाख्या (°प-आख्°), f., scil. गति, epithet of one of the seven divisions of the planetary courses (according to the Parāśara-tantra extending over the constellations Hasta, Maitra, and Vi-śākhā). —पापाङ्कुशा (°प-अङ्°), f., N. of the eleventh day in the light half of the month Āśvina. —पापाचार (°प-आच्°), अस्, आ, अम्, ill-conducted, following evil courses, practising evil, living an evil life, vicious. —पापात्मन् (°प-आत्°), आ, आ, अ, evil-minded, wicked; (आ), m. a sinner, reprobate, wretch; (opposed to धर्मात्मन्।) —पापाधम (°प-अध्°), अस्, आ, अम्, the lowest of the wicked, exceedingly low or wicked. —पापानुव-सित (°प-अन्°), अस्, आ, अम्, addicted to sin, sinful. —पापान्त (°प-अन्°), अम्, n., N. of a Tīrtha (‘where sins come to an end’). —पापापनुत्ति (°प-अप्°), इस्, f. ‘removal of sins,’ expiation. —पा-पावहीयम् (°प-अव्°), ind., Ved. wrongfully staying away or remaining behind. —पापाशय (°प-आश्°), अस्, आ, अम्, evil-intentioned, wicked, sinful. —पापाह (°प-अह°), अम्, n., Ved. an unlucky day. —पापाहि (°प-अहि), इस्, m. a snake, serpent. —पापोक्त (°प-उक्°), अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. addressed in ill-omened words.
पापक: पापक, अस्, इका or अकी, अम्, bad, evil, wicked; (अम्), n. evil, wrong, wickedness, sin; (अस्), m. a wicked person, rascal; an evil or malignant planet.
पापल: पापल, अस्, आ, अम्, imparting or incurring guilt; (अम्), n. a particular measure.
पापिन्: पापिन्, ई, इनी, इ, wicked, sinful, bad; a sinner, criminal.
पापिष्ठ: पापिष्ठ, अस्, आ, अम्, worst, lowest, most wicked; exceedingly bad, very wicked. —पापिष्ठ-तम, अस्, आ, अम्, worst, most wicked; worse, more wicked. —पापिष्ठ-तर, अस्, आ, अम्, worse, more wicked; the very worst; exceedingly wicked.
पापीय: पापीय, अस्, आ, अम्, worse, &c.; (a contracted form of पापीयस् below.)
पापीयस्: पापीयस्, आन्, असी, अस्, worse, worse off, more wretched or miserable; lower, poorer; more wicked; very bad or wicked, very criminal; मारः पापीयान्, (with Buddhists) the evil spirit, the devil; (अस्), m. a wicked man, wretch, villain. —पापीयस्-तर, अस्, आ, अम्, = पापीयस्. —पापीयस्-त्व, अम्, n. the state of being very wicked, great wickedness.
पाप्मन्: पाप्मन्, आ, m. evil, unhappiness, evil plight, suffering; crime, evil, sin, wickedness; (आ, आ, अ), injurious, hurtful, evil.
पापापुरी: पापापुरी पापापुरी, f. = पावापुरी, f., N. of a town near Rāja-gṛha.
पामन्: पामन् पामन्, आ, m. (fr. rt. पै), a kind of skin disease, cutaneous eruption, herpes, scab. —पाम-घ्न, अस्, ई, अम्, destroying the scab; (अस्), m. sulphur; (ई), f. a species of plant (= क-टुका). —पाम-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, diseased with herpes.
पामन: पामन, अस्, आ, अम्, diseased with herpes. —पा-मनम्-भावुक, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. becoming dis-eased with herpes.
पामर: पामर, अस्, आ, अम्, diseased with herpes, scabby; wicked, vile; low, vulgar, base; stupid; (अस्), m. a man of the lowest extraction, a man engaged in any degrading occupation; an idiot, fool; a wicked man; (अम्), n. evil, bad character, wickedness. —पामरोद्धारा (°र-उद्°), f. ‘removing herpes,’ a species of plant (= गुडूची).
पामा: पामा, f. herpes, scab (enumerated among the forms of so-called mild leprosy). —पामारि (°मा-अरि), इस्, m. ‘enemy of the scab,’ sulphur.
पाम्प: पाम्प पाम्प, अस्, ई, अम्, belonging to or situated on the river Pampā.
पाम्पन: पाम्पन, अस्, ई, अम्, belonging or relating to the river Pampā.
पाय: पाय पाय, अम्, n. (fr. rt. 1. पा), water. —पाय-गुण्ड, अस्, m., N. of the author of a com-mentary on the Laghu-śabdendu-śekhara.
पायक: पायक, अस्, इका, अम्, drinking; [cf. तैल-पायिका।]
पायन: पायन, अम्, n. the causing or giving to drink; (Sāy.) = 1. पान, a beverage; (आ), f. causing to drink; watering, moistening.
पायिन्: पायिन्, ई, इनी, इ, (at the end of a comp.) drinking; [cf. कुण्ड-प्°, क्षीर-प्°, चन्द्रिका-प्°।]
पायु: 1. पायु, उस्, m. the anus. —पायु-क्षालन-भूमि, इस्, f. or पायु-क्षालन-वेश्मन्, अ, n. a water-closet, privy. —पायु-भेद, अस्, m., Ved. (in astrol.) N. of two ways in which an eclipse terminates.
पायु 2. पायु, उस्, m. (fr. rt. 3. पा; for 1. see above), Ved. a guard, protector; N. of a man; (अवस्), m. pl. protecting powers or actions.
पाय्य: 1. पाय्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be drunk, to be caused to drink; (अम्), n. water; drinking.
2. पाय्य (for 1. see above), protection (at the end of a comp.; cf. नृ-प्°).
पाय्य 3. पाय्य, अम्, n. measure; practice, profession.
पाय्य 4. पाय्य, अस्, आ, अम्, low, vile, repre-hensible, contemptible.
पायस: पायस पायस, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. पयस्), pre-pared with or made of milk or water; (अस्, अम्), m. n. food prepared with milk, rice boiled in milk; an oblation of milk, rice, and sugar; the resin of Pinus Longifolia; turpentine; (अम्), n. milk; a kind of divine beverage, nectar (Rām. I. 15, 8). —पायस-दग्ध, अस्, आ, अम्, scalded by milk-porridge.
पायसिक: पायसिक, अस्, ई, अम्, fond of boiled milk, re-lating to any mixture of milk, &c.
पायिक: पायिक पायिक, अस्, m. a foot-soldier, foot-man; (probably a corruption of पादातिक।)
पार: पार पार, अस्, m. (fr. rt. 1. पृ or rt. पॄ), cross-ing [cf. दुष्-प्°]; the further shore or opposite bank of a river; the further side, concluding bound; the end or limit of anything, the utmost reach or extent; quicksilver; N. of a sage, a son of Pṛthu-ṣeṇa and father of Nīpa; of a son of Samara and father of Pṛthu; of a son of Aṅga and father of Divi-ratha; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a class of deities under the ninth Manu; (आ), f., N. of a river (said to flow from the Pāriyātra mountains or the central and western portion of the Vindhya chain); (ई), f. a quantity of water; a small water-jar, drinking-vessel, glass, cup; a milk-pail; a rope for tying an elephant's feet; pollen; (अम्), n. (according to some also अस्, m.), the further or opposite end or bank of a river; the totality of an object, the fullest extent (with gen., e. g. तमसस्, of darkness; कारणानाम्, of tor-tures); extremity, end, aim (in this sense also m.); पारं गम्, to cross over; to fulfil (e. g. प्रतिज्ञा-याः पारं स गतः, he fulfilled his promise); to become proficient in; पारं नी, to bring to a close; [cf. पर, परम्; Gr. πόρο-ς, πέρα πέρᾱν, περαίνω, πείρω, περαῖο-ς, περά-τη, Πειραιεύ-ς, πέρας, πεῖραρ, ἀπειρέσ-ιο-ς; Lat. per; Lith. per, ‘across;’ Slav. polŭ, ‘the opposite bank.’] —पार-काम, अस्, आ, अम्, desirous of reaching the opposite bank. —पार-ग, अस्, आ, अम्, going to the opposite shore, crossing over, going through or over or across or to the end, ferrying across, intending to cross; one who has arrived at the end, accomplishing, one who has accomplished or completely mastered, completely familiar or conversant with, knowing thoroughly, well versed in (with gen. or loc. or in a comp., e. g. वेदानाम् पारगः, well versed in the Vedas; प्रतिज्ञा-प्°, fulfilling or keeping a promise); pro-foundly learned; going over or beyond the world; (अम्), n. keeping, fulfilling. —पार-गत, अस्, आ, अम्, or पार-गामिन्, ई, इनी, इ, one who has reached the opposite shore, passed over in safety, crossed; passed beyond the world, pure, holy; (अस्), m. (with Jainas) an Arhat or deified saint and teacher. —पार-गति, इस्, f. going through, reading, studying through. —पार-गमन, अम्, n. reaching the opposite shore, crossing, going to the end. —पार-चर, अस्, ई, अम्, arriving at the opposite shore, crossing over. —पार-तस्, ind., Ved. on the opposite bank, on the further side. —पार-दण्डक, अस्, m. (perhaps a Vṛddhied form fr. पर + दण्डक), N. of a country (part of Orissa). —पार-दर्शक, अस्, आ, अम्, showing the opposite bank. —पार-दर्शन, अस्, आ, अम्, beholding the opposite bank or shore, able to survey all things. —पार-दृश्वन्, आ, अरी, अ, one who has seen the opposite bank, completely familiar with, knowing thoroughly; long-sighted, far-seeing, wise. —पार-ध्वज, आस्, m. pl. ‘banners of the further shore,’ N. of certain banners brought from beyond the sea (from Ceylon) and borne in procession by the kings of Kaśmīra. —पार-नेतृ, ता, त्री, तृ, bringing to the further shore. —पारम्-इत, अस्, आ, अम्, gone to the opposite bank; crossed, traversed; transcendant (as spiritual knowledge); (आ), f. (probably a contracted form for पारमित-ता), coming to the opposite bank, complete attainment, perfection (the Buddhists enumerate six or sometimes ten Pāramitās or perfections as belonging to a Bodhi-sattva). —पारापार (°र-अप्°), अम्, n. = पारावार, the nearer and further bank, both banks, (a various reading for पारावार, q. v.); (अस्), m. the sea, ocean. —पारायण (°र-अय्°), अम्, n. going over, going across; reading from one end to the other, reading through, perusing, studying, study; reading a Purāṇa or causing it to be read; the whole, totality, entireness, completeness [cf. धातु-प्°, नाम-प्°]; N. of a grammatical work; (ई), f. a N. of the goddess Sarasvatī; an act, action; considering, medi-tating; light. —पारायण-माहात्म्य, अम्, n., N. of a section. of the Pātāla-khaṇḍa of the Pādma-Purāṇa. —पारायणिक, अस्, ई, अम्, reading to (any one), teaching how to pronounce; (अस्), m. a lec-turer, reader of the Purāṇas; a pupil, scholar; (आस्), m. pl. epithet of a particular school of grammarians. —पारायणीय, अम्, n., N. of a grammar. —पा-रावार (°र-अव्°), अम्, n. the further and the nearer bank or shore, the opposite banks (e. g. पारावारस्य नौः, a boat which plies from one side to the other); (अस्), m. the sea, ocean; [cf. पारापार।] —पारावारीण, अस्, आ, अम्, on both sides of a river, &c., one who goes to both sides. —पारे-गङ्गम्, ind. on the other side of the Gaṅgā, beyond the Ganges. —पारे-विशोक, N. of a place. —पारे-सिन्धु, ind. on the other side of the Sindhu, beyond the Indus.
पारक: 1. पारक, अस्, ई, अम् (for 2. see p. 567, col. 1), carrying over, bearing across, saving, delivering (in उग्र-प्°, q. v.); enabling to cross (a river or the world).
पारक 2. पारक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. rt. पॄ; for 1. see p. 566, col. 3), satisfying, pleasing; cherishing.
पारण: 1. पारण, अस्, आ, अम्, (for 2. see p. 567, col. 1), bringing over, carrying across, saving, deli-vering; (अम्), n. fulfilling, accomplishing; reading through, reading, studying; the complete text (of a book); (अम्, आ), n. f., also व्रत-पारण, concluding a fast, eating or drinking after a fast, breakfast; [cf. शोणित-प्°।] —पारण-कर्मन्, अ, n. exercise in reading, mode of reading.
2. पारण, अस्, m. (for 1. see p. 566, col. 3), satis-fying, satisfaction; a cloud.
पारणीय: पारणीय, अस्, आ, अम्, having an attainable end, capable of being completed or brought to an end.
पारय: 1. पारय, Nom. P. A. पारयति, -ते, &c., to bring over, lead over; to be able; (this is also regarded as the Caus. of rt. 1. पृ, q. v.)
2. पारय, अस्, आ, अम्, able, adequate, fit for.
3. पारय, अस्, आ, अम्, (for 1. and 2. see p. 566, col. 3), satisfying, filling.
पारय 1. and 2. पारय, पारयत्, पार-यिष्णु। See p. 566, col. 3, and col. 1. of this p.
पारयत्: 1. पारयत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, being able, competent.
2. पारयत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, satisfying, filling.
पारयिष्णु: 1. पारयिष्णु, उस्, उस्, उ (for 2. see s. v.), Ved. bringing to a successful issue, causing to succeed, victorious.
2. पारयिष्णु, उस्, उस्, उ, gratifying, pleasing, satisfying.
पारीण: पारीण, अस्, आ, अम्, being on the other or opposite side; crossing to the other or opposite side; (at the end of a comp.) completely familiar with, well acquainted with [cf. त्रिवर्ग-प्°]; (अस्), m., N. of a man (= पारिण).
पारीय: पारीय, अस्, आ, अम्, (at the end of a comp.) com-pletely familiar with, well acquainted with.
पार्य: पार्य, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. being on the opposite side or bank; upper; last, final; giving the last stroke, decisive (e. g. पार्ये धने, Ved. in a decisive battle); causing to succeed, helping through; effec-tual, efficient; (अम्), n. end; decision.
पारक्य: पारक्य पारक्य, अस्, आ, अम्, = परकीय, be-longing to another or a stranger, alien (opposed to स्व); intended for others, serving others; belonging to an enemy, hostile, inimical; (अस्), m. an enemy; (अम्), n. doing anything for the sake of future hap-piness, pious conduct.
पारग्रामिक: पारग्रामिक पारग्रामिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. पर + ग्राम), ‘belonging to another village,’ hos-tile, inimical, (पारग्रामिकं विधिम् आचिकीर्षति, he is about to perform hostile action, i. e. prepares for hostilities.)
पारज्: पारज् पारज्, क्, m. (said to be fr. पार), gold.
पारजायिक: पारजायिक पारजायिक, अस्, m. (fr. पर + जाया), one who intrigues with another's wife, an adulterer.
पारटीट: पारटीट पारटीट, अस्, m. (connected with पार?), a stone, rock; [cf. पारारुक।]
पारत: पारत 1. पारत, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. पर-तस्), see Vārttikā to Pāṇ. IV. 2, 104; (Ved.) N. of a people or country.
पारत 2. पारत, अस्, m. quicksilver; [cf. पारद।]
पारतक: पारतक, आस्, m. pl., N. of a people.
पारतन्त्रिक: पारतन्त्रिक पारतन्त्रिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. पर-तन्त्र), belonging to or enjoined by the religious treatises of others.
पारतन्त्र्य: पारतन्त्र्य, अम्, n. the being subject to another, dependence, subservience, slavery.
पारत्रिक: पारत्रिक पारत्रिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. पर-त्र), relating to another world, belonging to the next world, advantageous in the future life.
पारत्र्य: पारत्र्य, अस्, आ, अम्, relating to the next world; rewarded in a future state (according to Kullūka = परलोक-फल).
पारद: पारद पारद, अस्, m. quicksilver; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a barbarous people (described in Manu X. 44. as a Kṣatriya tribe degraded to Śūdras by neglect of duties; cf. 2. पारत).
पारदारिक: पारदारिक पारदारिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. पर-दार), intriguing with another's wife; relating to another's wife; (अस्), m. an adulterer.
पारदारिन्: पारदारिन्, ई, इणी, इ, intriguing with another's wife; (perhaps incorrectly for पर-दारिन्।)
पारदार्य: पारदार्य, अम्, n. intriguing with another's wife, adultery.
पारदेशिक: पारदेशिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. पर-देश), outlandish, foreign, abroad; (अस्), m. a traveller; a foreigner.
पारदेश्य: पारदेश्य, अस्, शी, अम्, belonging to or coming from a foreign country, foreign; (अस्), m. a traveller, one who has gone to a foreign country; a foreigner; [cf. Lat. per-egrinus.]
पारधेनु: पारधेनु, उस्, or पारधेनुक, अस्, m., N. of a low mixed caste, an Āyogava (q. v.).
पारम्परीण: पारम्परीण, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. परम्-परा), passing from one to another, handed down from father to son, hereditary.
पारम्परीय: पारम्परीय, अस्, ई, अम्, handed down, tra-ditional.
पारम्पर्य: पारम्पर्य, अस्, ई, अम्, one following the other; (अम्), n. uninterrupted series, continuous order or hereditary succession; traditional instruction, tradition; intercession, intermediation; (एण), ind. successively. —पारम्पर्य-क्रमागत (°म-आग्°), or पारम्-पर्यागत (°य-आग्°), अस्, आ, अम्, derived from tradition. —पारम्पर्योपदेश (°य-उप्°), अस्, m. traditional instruction.
पारलोक्य: पारलोक्य, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. पर-लोक), relating to the next world.
पारलौकिक: पारलौकिक, अस्, ई, अम्, relating to the next world (e. g. सहायः पारलौकिकः, a companion on the way to the next world); epithet of a place where pearls are found and of the pearls found there (Ved.); (अम्), n. things or circumstances relat-ing to the next world.
पारवर्ग्य: पारवर्ग्य, अस्, आ, अम्, (fr. पर + वर्ग), be-longing to another party, siding with the enemy.

पारीरण: पारीरण पारीरण, अस्, m. = परीरण, q. v.
पारु: पारु पारु, उस्, m. (said to be fr. rt. 3. पा), the sun; fire (= पेरु).
पारुच्छेप: पारुच्छेप पारुच्छेप, अस्, ई, अम्, derived from Parucchepa; भारद्वाजम् पारुच्छेपम्, N. of a Sāman.
पारुच्छेपि: पारुच्छेपि, इस्, m. a patronymic from Parucchepa.
पारुषक: पारुषक पारुषक, अस्, or अम्, m. or n. (?), a species of flower; [cf. परूषक।]
पारुषेय: पारुषेय पारुषेय, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. परुष), Ved. spotted, freckled.
पारुष्य: पारुष्य, अम्, n. roughness [cf. त्वक्-प्°], harsh-ness; harshness of language, abuse, reproach, con-tumelious or scurrilous language, opprobrious or unfriendly speech, insult; violence (in word or deed, cf. दण्ड-प्°, वाक्-प्°); squalor; the forest or grove of Indra; aloe wood or Agallochum; (अस्), m. a N. of Bṛhas-pati, the planet Jupiter.
पारुष्ण: पारुष्ण पारुष्ण, अस्, m., Ved. a kind of bird.
पारेगङ्गम्: पारेगङ्गम् पारे-गङ्गम्, पारे-विशोक, पारे-सिन्धु। See under पार।
पारेरक: पारेरक पारेरक, अस्, m. a sword, sci-mitar (?).
पारोक्ष: पारोक्ष पारोक्ष, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. परोक्ष), undiscernible, unintelligible, obscure, mysterious.
पारोक्ष्य: पारोक्ष्य, अस्, आ, अम्, undiscernible, invisible, hidden; (अम्), n. mysteriousness, mystery.
पारोवर्य: पारोवर्य पारोवर्य, अम्, n. (fr. परो-ऽव-रम्), tradition.
पार्घट: पार्घट पार्घट, अम्, n. ashes, = अर्घट; [cf. पार्पर।]
पार्जन्य: पार्जन्य पार्जन्य, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. पर्जन्य), belonging to Parjanya.
पार्ण: पार्ण पार्ण, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. पर्ण), made or consisting of leaves, leafy; raised from leaves (as a tax); made of the wood of the Butea Frondosa; (अस्), m. a patronymic.
पार्णवल्कि: पार्णवल्कि, इस्, m. (fr. पर्ण-वल्क), a patro-nymic of Ni-gada.
पार्थ: पार्थ 1. पार्थ, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. पृथि), Ved. an epithet of twelve sacred texts, ascribed to Pṛthi Vainya, repeated during the ceremony of unction in the Rāja-sūya sacrifice; (अस्), m. a patronymic of Tānva; (अम्), n., N. of several Sāmans.

पार्थ 2. पार्थ, अस्, m. (fr. rt. पृथ् for प्रथ् and connected with पृथु, wide), a prince, king (= पार्थिव); (fr. पृथा), a metronymic of Yudhi-ṣṭhira, Bhīma-sena, and Arjuna, especially of the last; N. of a son of Paṅgu and king of Kaśmīra; N. of a man; the plant Terminalia Arjuna; (आस्), m. pl. an epithet of the five sons of Pāṇḍu. —पार्थ-ज, अस्, m. the son of Pārtha. —पार्थ-पुर, अम्, n., N. of a city near the con-fluence of the Go-dāvarī and Vi-darbhā. —पार्थ-मय, अस्, ई, अम्, consisting of sons of Pṛthā. —पार्थ-सारथि, इस्, m., N. of the author of the Tantra-ratna. —पार्थसारथि-मिश्र, अस्, m., N. of a commentator on Jaimini's Nyāya-sūtras. —पार्-थानुग (°थ-अन्°), अस्, आ, अम्, followed by (Pārtha, i. e.) Arjuna.
पार्थ्य: पार्थ्य, अस्, m., Ved. a patronymic from Pṛthi.
पार्थव: पार्थव, अस्, ई, अम्, belonging or peculiar to Pṛthu; (अम्), n. width, greatness, immensity.
पार्थवि: पार्थवि, an earthy substance, rotten wood; (pro-bably a wrong reading for पार्थिव।)
पार्थिव: पार्थिव, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. पृथिवी for पृथ्वी, f. of पृथु), earthen, earthly, terrestrial, relating to the earth, springing or derived from the earth, made of earth, earthy; ruling or possessing the earth; fit for kings or princes, royal, princely; अ-पार्थिव, unearthly, i. e. heavenly, celestial; (अस्), m. a dweller on the earth, inhabitant of the earth; a lord of the earth, king, prince, sovereign, warrior; an earthen vessel; the 19th (or 53rd) year in Jupiter's cycle of 60 years; (आस्), m. pl. a patronymic; (ई), f. ‘earth-born,’ an epithet of Sītā; of Lakṣmī; (अम्), n. an earthy substance; (आनि), n. pl., Ved. the regions of the earth (Sāy. = पृथिव्याम् भवानि स्थानानि). —पार्थिव-ता, f. or पार्थिव-त्व, अम्, n. the dignity or rank of king, royalty. —पार्थिव-नन्-दिनी, f. the daughter of a king. —पार्थिवर्षभ (°व-ऋ°), अस्, m. ‘king-bull,’ an excellent king. —पार्थिव-श्रेष्ठ, अस्, m. best of kings, an excellent sovereign. —पार्थिव-सुता or पार्थिवात्-मजा (°व-आत्°), f. the daughter of a king. —पार्-थिवाधम (°व-अध्°), अस्, m. the lowest or meanest of kings. —पार्थिवेन्द्र (°व-इन्°), अस्, m. the chief or greatest of princes.
पार्थक्य: पार्थक्य पार्थक्य, अम्, n. (fr. पृथक्), severalty, individuality, separation, separateness, sin-gleness, difference, variety.
पार्थुरश्म: पार्थुरश्म पार्थुरश्म, अम्, n. (fr. पृथु-रश्मि), Ved. epithet of various Sāmans.
पार्पर: पार्पर पार्पर, अस्, m. a handful of rice; consumption (= क्षय-रोग); a filament of the Nauclea Cadamba; ashes; = कीनाश; = गदान्तर (a kind of disease ?); a N. of Yama.
पार्यन्तिक: पार्यन्तिक पार्यन्तिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. पर्य्-अन्त), final, concluding, last.
पार्व: पार्व पार्व, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. पर्वन्), = पार्-वण; (probably an incorrect form.)
पार्वण: पार्वण, अस्, ई, अम्, belonging or relating to a division of time or of the month; increasing, waxing full (as the moon); (अस्), m. a kind of deer; the general funeral ceremony to be offered to all the Manes at the Parvan (or conjunction of the sun and moon, at which double oblations are offered, three cakes to the father, paternal grandfather and great-grandfather, and three to the maternal grandfather, his father and grandfather; and the crumbs of each set to the remoter ancestors in each line).
पार्वायनान्तीय: पार्वायनान्तीय, अस्, आ, अम्, (fr. पर्वन् + अय-नान्त), occurring at the end of a Parvan or solstice (as a sacrifice &c.).
पार्वत: पार्वत पार्वत, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. पर्वत), being or living in the mountains, growing on or coming from the mountains, consisting of moun-tains, mountainous; (अस्), m. the tree Melia Sem-pervirens (= महा-निम्ब); (ई), f. a mountain stream; a female cowherd or Gopī; a N. of Durgā (as being the daughter of Hima-vat the king of the snowy mountains); N. of a cave in mount Meru; of various women (named after the goddess); an epithet of Draupadī (incorrectly for पार्षती); a kind of fragrant earth; a red clay commonly called Saurāṣṭrī or Surat earth; N. of various plants; the olibanum tree, Boswellia Thurifera; Grislea To-mentosa; = Celtis Orientalis; = क्षुद्र-पाषाण-भेदा; = जीवनी। —पार्वती-क्षेत्र, अम्, n. ‘dis-trict of Pārvatī (Durgā),’ N. of one of the four especially sacred districts of Orissa. —पार्वती-नन्-दन, अस्, m. ‘son of Pārvatī,’ an epithet of Kārtti-keya. —पार्वती-पश्चात्ताप-वर्णन, अम्, n., N. of the sixth chapter of the Gīta-gaṅgādhara, a poem by Kalyāṇa. —पार्वती-प्रवर्तन, अम्, n., N. of the ninth chapter of the Gīta-girīśa, a poem by Rāma. —पार्वती-प्रसादन, अम्, n., N. of the fifth chapter of the Gīta-gaṅgādhara. —पार्वती-मोक्षण, अम्, n., N. of a chapter of the Gaṇeśa-Purāṇa. —पार्वतीश्वर-लिङ्ग (°ती-ईश्°), अम्, n., N. of a Liṅga. —पार्वती-सम्प्रदान, अम्, n., N. of a chapter of the Brahma-vaivarta-Purāṇa.
पार्वतायन: पार्वतायन, अस्, m. a patronymic; N. of a chamberlain.
पार्वति: पार्वति, इस्, m. a patronymic of Dakṣa.
पार्वतिक: पार्वतिक, अम्, n. a multitude of mountains, mountain-range.
पार्वतीय: पार्वतीय, अस्, ई, अम्, living or dwelling in the mountains, mountainous; (अस्), m. a mountaineer; epithet of a particular sovereign ruling in the moun-tains; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a mountain tribe.
पार्वतेय: पार्वतेय, अस्, ई, अम्, belonging or relating to the mountains, mountain-born; (अस्), m., N. of a prince of mountaineers; a species of culinary plant bearing a pungent fruit; (ई), f. the smaller or upper mill-stone; (अम्), n. antimony (= सौवीराञ्जन).
पार्शव: पार्शव 1. पार्शव, अस्, m. (fr. 1. पर्शु), a prince of the Parśus.
पार्शव 2. पार्शव, अस्, m. a warrior armed with an axe.
पार्श्व: पार्श्व, अस्, अम्, m. n. the region of the ribs or the part of the body below the armpit; the side, flank (either of animate or inanimate objects); a side of any square figure; a curved knife (Ved.); (अस्), m., N. of an ancient Buddhist teacher; (with Jainas) N. of the twenty-third Arhat of the present Ava-sarpiṇī; (औ), m. du. heaven and earth; (अम्), n. a multitude of ribs, the thorax; the extremity of the fore-axle nearest the wheel to which the outside horses of a four-horse chariot are attached; a fraudu-lent or crooked expedient, dishonourable means; (आनि), n. pl. the ribs (Ved.); (ए), ind. at the side, near, on, upon, (opposed to दूर-तस्, दूरे); aside; (अयोस्), ind. on both sides; (आत्), ind. away from; (अम्), ind. near to, to, towards; (अस्, आ, अम्), near, proximate, by the side of. —पार्श्व-ग, अस्, आ, अम्, going at the side (of any one), accompanying, being in close proximity to, an attendant; (आस्), m. pl. attendants, retinue. —पार्श्व-गत, अस्, आ, अम्, being at the side, attending, accompanying, being close to or beside; sheltered, screening. —पार्श्व-गमन, अम्, n. the act of going by the side, accompanying. —पार्श्व-चर, अस्, m. an attendant; (आस्), m. pl. attendants, retinue. —पार्श्व-तस्, ind. by or from the side, at the side, near, sideways, aside. —पार्श्व-द, अस्, m. ‘turning the side towards another,’ an attendant; (आस्), m. pl. attendants, retinue. —पार्श्व-दाह, अस्, m. a burning pain in the side. —पार्श्व-देश, अस्, m. the region of the ribs, the side. —पार्श्व-द्रुम, आस्, m. pl. the trees at the side, the trees on every side. —पार्श्व-नाथ, अस्, m. (with Jainas) N. of an Arhat; the Jaina pontiff. —पार्श्वनाथ-काव्य, अम्, n., N. of a poem by Padma-sundara celebrating the preceding Arhat. —पार्श्व-परिवर्तन, अम्, n. ‘the turning round on the other side or from one side to the other,’ epithet of a festival on the eleventh day of the light half of the month Bhādra (Viṣṇu being sup-posed to turn upon the other side in his sleep on this day). —पार्श्व-परिवर्तिन्, ई, इनी, इ, being or going by the side (of any one). —पार्श्व-पिप्पल, अम्, n. a species of Harītakī (= Hindī गजहड्). —पार्श्व-भाग, अस्, m. ‘side-portion,’ the side, flank (of an elephant). —पार्श्व-रुज्, क्, f. pain in the side. —पार्श्व-वक्त्र, अस्, m. whose face is in his side,’ N. of a being attendant upon Śiva (Hari-vaṃśa 14851). —पार्श्व-वर्तिन्, ई, इनी, इ, standing by the side, an attendant; situated at the side, adjacent; (इनस्), m. pl. attendants, retinue. —पार्-श्व-विवर्तिन्, ई, इनी, इ, being by the side of, living with. —पार्श्व-शय, अस्, आ, अम्, lying or sleeping on the side; sleeping at the side. —पार्श्व-शायिन्, ई, इनी, इ, ‘lying on the side,’ epithet of a particular position of the moon. —पार्श्व-शूल, अस्, m. a shooting pain in the side, spasm of the chest, stitch; pleurisy. —पार्श्व-संस्थ, अस्, आ, अम्, lying on the side. —पार्श्व-सूत्रक, अस्, or अम्, m. or n. (?), a kind of ornament. —पार्श्व-स्थ, अस्, आ, अम्, standing at the side or next to, being near or close to, adjacent, proximate; (अस्), m. an associate, com-panion; a stage manager's assistant (said to serve as a sort of chorus to the Indian drama, being some-times an actor in the prelude and interpreter of the plot). —पार्श्व-स्थित, अस्, आ, अम्, standing at the side, being near or close to. —पार्श्वानुचर (°व-अन्°), अस्, m. ‘attending at the side,’ an attendant, body-servant, lackey. —पार्श्वायात (°व-आय्°), अस्, आ, अम्, one who has approached close to. —पार्श्वा-सन्न (°व-आस्°), अस्, आ, अम्, standing by the side, standing next, present. —पार्श्वासीन (°व-आस्°), अस्, आ, अम्, sitting by the side. —पार्श्वास्थि (°व-अस्°), इ, n. ‘side-bone,’ a rib. —पार्श्वैकादशी (°व-एक्°), f., N. of a particular festival (= पार्श्व-परिवर्-तन). —पार्श्वोदर-प्रिय (°व-उद्°), अस्, m. ‘fond of (moving) sideways on the belly,’ a crab.
पार्श्वक: पार्श्वक, अस्, m. a rib; (अस्, आ, अम्), one who seeks wealth or other objects by dishonest or indirect or side means; a pilferer, swindler.
पार्श्वतीय: पार्श्वतीय, अस्, आ, अम्, (fr. पार्श्व-तस्), being on or belonging to the side, situated at the side.
पार्श्विक: पार्श्विक, अस्, ई, अम्, lateral, belonging to the side; (अस्), m. a sidesman, partisan; an associate, companion; a juggler; one who seeks money by dishonest means; N. of an ancient Buddhist teacher.
पार्श्व्य: पार्श्व्य, औ, m. du. heaven and earth (a various reading for पार्श्वौ).
पार्षकि: पार्षकि पार्षकि, इस्, m. a patronymic.
पार्षत: पार्षत पार्षत, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. पृषत), belonging to the spotted antelope, made of the skin of the spotted antelope; (अस्), m. a patronymic of Dru-pada and his son Dhṛṣṭa-dyumna; (ई), f. a patronymic of Draupadī; an epithet of Durgā (in this sense a wrong reading for पार्वती); N. of two plants, Boswellia Thurifera; = जीवनी।
पार्षद्: पार्षद् पार्षद्, त्, f. (for परि-षद?), an assembly; (दस्), m. pl. the attendants or retinue of a god.
पार्षद: पार्षद, अस्, m. (fr. पर्षद्), an associate, companion, attendant; a train, retinue (especially of a god); a person present in a congregation or assembly, a spectator; (perhaps) a councillor, dis-tinguished personage; (अम्), n. a text-book received by any particular grammatical school, a N. given to the Prātiśākhyas; N. of a work on ceremonies. —पार्षद-ता, f. the office of an attendant (espe-cially of the attendant of a deity).
पार्षदीय: पार्षदीय, अस्, आ, अम्, conformable to the received text-book of any particular grammatical school.
पार्षद्य: पार्षद्य, अस्, m. = पारिषद्य, a member of an assembly or council, assessor; (आस्), m. pl. the attendants or retinue of a god (especially of Śiva).
पार्षद्वाण: पार्षद्वाण पार्षद्वाण, अस्, m. (fr. पृषद्-वाण), N. of a man.
पार्षिका: पार्षिका पार्षिका, f., N. of a woman.
पार्ष्टेय: पार्ष्टेय पार्ष्टेय, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. पृष्टि), being within the ribs.
पार्ष्ठिक: पार्ष्ठिक पार्ष्ठिक, अस्, ई, अम्, Ved. being after the manner of the Pṛṣṭhya (Ṣaḍ-aha).
पार्ष्णि: पार्ष्णि पार्ष्णि, इस्, m. f., rarely पार्ष्णी, f. (said to be fr. rt. पृष्), the heel; the extremity of the fore-axle to which the outside horses of a four-horse chariot are attached (the two inner horses being harnessed to the धुर् or chariot-pole); the rear of an army; the back; a kick; enquiry, asking (?); (इस्), f. a foolish or licentious woman; a N. of Kuntī the wife of Pāṇḍu. —पार्ष्णि-क्षेम, अस्, m., N. of a divinity. —पार्ष्णि-ग्रह, अस्, आ, अम्, seizing from behind, threatening from behind; (अस्), m. a follower. —पार्ष्णि-ग्रहण, अम्, n. attacking or threatening (an enemy) in the rear. —पार्ष्णि-ग्राह, अस्, आ, अम्, attacking or menac-ing (an enemy) in the rear; (अस्), m. an enemy in the rear; a commander in the rear of an army; an ally who supports a prince (Manu VII. 207). —पार्ष्णि-त्र, अम्, n. ‘rear-protecting,’ a rear-guard, reserve, a body of forces in the rear. —पार्ष्-णि-वाह्, ट्, ऊही, ट्, or पार्ष्णि-वाह, अस्, आ, अम्, draw-ing (i. e. harnessed to) the extremities of the axle-tree; (अस्), m. an outside horse. —पार्ष्णि-सारथि, इस्, m. a charioteer who drives one of the outside horses; (ई), m. du. the two charioteers who drive the outer horses attached to the extremities of the axle-tree.
पाल्: पाल् पाल्। See Caus. of rt. 3. पा।
पाल: पाल, अस्, m. a guard, guardian, protector, nourisher, keeper; a herdsman; a protector of the earth, a prince; a spitting-pot, spittoon; N. of a Nāga of the race of Vāsuki; of a prince; (ई), f. a herdsman's wife; [cf. पालि।] —पाल-कवि-राज, अस्, m., N. of a poet (also called Śrī-pāla-kavi-rāja). —पाल-काव्य, अम्, n. ‘the poem of Pāla,’ N. of a work. —पाल-घ्न, अस्, m. a mushroom. —पाल-बणिज्, क्, m. = कन्या-पाल; (a wrong form for पान-बणिज्।) —पाली-व्रत, अम्, n., N. of a par-ticular religious observance.
पालक: पालक, अस्, इका, अम्, guarding, protecting, nourish-ing; (अस्), m. a guardian, protector, cherisher, nourisher; a foster-father; a prince, ruler, sovereign; a horse-keeper, a groom; one who maintains or observes; N. of several princes; a species of plant with a poisonous bulb, Plumbago Zeylanica; a horse. —पालक-गोत्र, अम्, n. the family or tribe of one's adoptive parents. —पालकाख्या (°क-आख्°), f., N. of the mother of Dhanvantari.
पालन: पालन, अस्, ई, अम्, the act of protecting, guarding, fostering, nourishing, cherishing; (अम्), n. guarding, providing with a guardian, protecting, protection, preserving, cherishing, fostering, nourishing; main-taining, keeping, observing; the milk of a cow that has recently calved.
पालनीय: पालनीय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be guarded or protected, to be cherished or nourished; fit to be preserved or maintained; to be observed or respected.
पालयत्: पालयत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, guarding, protecting, cherishing.
पालयितृ: पालयितृ, ता, त्री, तृ, protecting, cherishing; a protector, guardian.

पिङ्ग, अस्, आ, अम्, reddish-brown, tawny, bright red, red, yellow; (अस्), m. tawny colour; (probably) N. of a herb (Ved.); a buffalo; a rat, mouse; N. of a man (Ved., cf. पैङ्गि, पैङ्गिन्); N. of one of the attendants of the Sun; (आ), f. a bow-string (Sāy. = पिङ्ग-वर्णा ज्या); a kind of yellow pig-ment [cf. गो-रोचना]; the stalk of Ferula Asa Fœ-tida; bamboo manna; turmeric, Indian saffron; an epithet of Durgā (?); a tubular vessel of the human body which according to the Yoga system is the channel of respiration and circulation for one side; (ई), f. a species of Mimosa, Mimosa Suma; (अम्), n. a young animal. —पिङ्ग-कपिशा, f. ‘tawny-brown,’ a species of cockroach. —पिङ्ग-चक्षुस्, उस्, m. ‘tawny-eyed,’ a crab. —पिङ्ग-जट, अस्, m. ‘having tawny braided hair,’ an epithet of Śiva. —पिङ्ग-तीर्थ, अम्, n., N. of a Tīrtha. —पिङ्ग-लोचन, अस्, आ, अम्, ‘tawny-eyed,’ having brown eyes. —पिङ्ग-सार, अस्, m. yellow orpiment. —पिङ्ग-स्फटिक, अस्, m. ‘yellow-crystal,’ a kind of gem (= गो-मेद). —पिङ्गाक्ष (°ग-अक्°), अस्, ई, अम्, ‘tawny-eyed,’ having reddish-brown eyes, red-eyed; (अस्), m. an ape; N. of Śiva; of a Rakṣas; of a wild man; of a bird; of one of the four sons of Droṇa; (ई), f., N. of a divinity; of one of the Mātṛs attending on Skanda. —पिङ्गास्य (°ग-आस्°), अस्, m. ‘tawny-faced,’ a species of fish, Pimelodius Pan-gasius. —पिङ्गेक्षण (°ग-ईक्°), अस्, ई, अम्, ‘tawny-eyed,’ having reddish-brown eyes; (अस्), m. an epithet of Śiva. —पिङ्गेश (°ग-ईश), अस्, m. ‘lord of the yellow hue,’ an epithet of fire.
पिचण्ड: पिचण्ड पिचण्ड, अस्, अम्, m. n. the belly; a particular part or limb of an animal.
पिचण्डक: पिचण्डक = पिचण्डे कुशलः, see Gaṇa to Pāṇ. V. 2, 64; (इका), f. the calf of the leg; the instep.
पिचण्डिन्: पिचण्डिन्, ई, इनी, इ, or पिचण्डिल, अस्, आ, अम्, big-bellied, corpulent.
पिचिण्ड: पिचिण्ड, अस्, m. the belly or abdomen; a parti-cular part of an animal. —पिचिण्ड-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, big-bellied, corpulent.
पिचिण्डिका: पिचिण्डिका, f. the calf of the leg; the instep.
पिचिण्डिल: पिचिण्डिल, अस्, आ, अम्, big-bellied, corpulent.
पिचु: पिचु पिचु, उस्, m. cotton; a sort of grain; the plant Vangueria Spinosa; a Karṣa or weight of two Tolas; a kind of leprosy; N. of an Asura; Bhairava or one of the eight faces of Bhairava. —पिचु-तूल, अम्, n. cotton. —पिचु-मन्द or पिचु-मर्द, अस्, m. the Nimb tree, Azadirachta Indica.
पिचव्य: पिचव्य, अस्, m. the cotton plant.
पिचुक: पिचुक, अस्, m. the plant Vangueria Spinosa; a species of tree.
पिचुल: पिचुल, अस्, m. cotton; the tamarisk, Tamarix Indica; another plant, Barringtonia Acutangula; a kind of cormorant or sea crow.
पिच्च्: पिच्च् पिच्च्, a various reading for rt. पिछ्, q. v.
पिच्चट: पिच्चट पिच्चट, अस्, आ, अम्, pressed flat, a substance pressed flat, cake [cf. तिल-प्°]; (अस्), m. inflammation of the eyes, ophthalmia; tin, lead.

पिच्चिट: पिच्चिट पिच्चिट or पिच्चिटक, अस्, m. a species of venomous insect.

पिछ्: पिछ् पिछ्, cl. 10. P. पिच्छयति, -यितुम्, to split, cut, divide; cl. 6. P. पिच्छति, पिच्छितुम्, to inflict pain; to obstruct, hinder.

पिच्छितिका: पिच्छितिका, f. = पिच्छिला, the Śiśu tree, Dalbergia Sissoo.

Basella Cordifolia. —पिच्छिल-त्वच्, क्, m. an orange-tree; orange-peel; a species of fruit tree (= धन्वन). —पिच्छिल-सार, अस्, m. the gum of Bombax Heptaphyllum.
पिच्छिलक: पिच्छिलक, अस्, m. a species of fruit tree (= धन्वन).
पिञ्छ: पिञ्छ, अम्, n. a wing (= पिच्छ).
पिजवन: पिजवन पिजवन, अस्, m., N. of a man.
पिजूल: पिजूल पिजूल, अस्, m., N. of a man.
पिञ्चदेव: पिञ्चदेव पिञ्च-देव, अस्, m., N. of a man.
पिञ्ज्: पिञ्ज् पिञ्ज्, cl. 2. A. पिङ्क्ते, पिपिञ्जे, पिञ्जिता, पिङ्क्तुम्, to tinge, dye, colour [cf. rt. 1. पिश्]; to sound; to touch; to join [cf. rt. 1. पृच्]; to adore; cl. 10. P. पिञ्जयति, -यितुम्, to kill, injure; to be strong; to give; to take; to dwell; to shine; to speak; to emit a sound; [cf. Lat. ping-ere.]
पिङ्गर: पिङ्गर, अस्, m., N. of a man.
पिङ्गल: पिङ्गल, अस्, आ, अम्, reddish-brown, tawny, brown, yellowish; (अस्), m. tawny colour, a dull brown or yellow hue; fire; a monkey; an ichneumon; a small kind of owl; a species of snake; a particular vegetable poison; (with Jainas) N. of a treasure; N. of one of Kuvera's divine treasures; of an attendant of the Sun; the sun (?); an epithet of Śiva or of a kindred being; N. of a Rudra; of a Yakṣa; of an attendant of Śiva; of a Dānava; of a fabulous being in the form of a Nāga (or serpent of the lower regions, the reputed author of the Chaṇḍas or treatise on prosody, regarded as one of the Vedāṅgas, and describing Prākṛt as well as Sanskrit metres; he is identified by some with Patañjali, the author of the celebrated commentary on Pāṇini called the Mahā-bhāṣya; by the Hindūs he is considered as a Muni or inspired and divine personage); N. of various ancient sages; N. of the fifty-first (or twenty-fifth) year in a sixty years' cycle of Jupiter; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a people; (आ), f. a species of bird, a kind of owl; the Śiśu tree, Dalbergia Sissoo; a kind of metal; a particular vessel of the body (the right of three canals running from the os coccygis to the head, which according to the anatomy of the Yoga school of philosophy are the chief passages of breath and air); the female elephant of the South quarter; N. of a courtezan who became remarkable for her piety; of an astrological house or period; heart-pea; (अम्), n. a particular metal (= राज-रीति), brass; yellow orpiment. —पिङ्गल-छन्दो-ग्रन्थ-टीका, f., N. of a commentary by Citra-sena on Piṅgala's Chandaḥ-śāstra. —पिङ्गल-नाग, अस्, m. the serpent-demon Piṅgala. —पिङ्गल-वृत्ति, इस्, f., N. of a commen-tary on Piṅgala's Chandaḥ-śāstra. —पिङ्गल-सार-विकाशिनी, f. ‘explaining the substance of Piṅgala,’ N. of a commentary by Ravi-kara on Piṅgala's Chandaḥ-śāstra. —पिङ्गलाक्ष (°ल-अक्°), अस्, m. ‘tawny-eyed,’ an epithet of Śiva. —पिङ्गला-तन्त्र and पिङ्गलामृत (°ल-अम्°), अम्, n., N. of two Tantras. —पिङ्गलेश्वर (°ल-ईश्°), अम्, n., N. of a Liṅga; (ई), f. a form of Dākṣāyaṇī. —पिङ्गलेश्-वर-तीर्थ, अम्, n., N. of a sacred bathing-place.
पिङ्गलक: पिङ्गलक, अस्, इका, अम्, (Ved.) reddish-brown, tawny; (अस्), m., N. of a Yakṣa; N. of a man; (आस्), m. pl., N. of his descendants; (इका), f. a kind of bee; a variety of the owl; a sort of crane; N. of a woman.
पिङ्गलित: पिङ्गलित, अस्, आ, अम्, made reddish-brown, become tawny.
पिङ्गाश: पिङ्गाश, अस्, m. the chief of a community of wild tribes; the head man or proprietor of a village; a kind of fish, Pimelodius Pangasius (= पिङ्गास्य); (ई), f. the indigo plant; (अम्), n. virgin gold.
पिञ्ज: पिञ्ज, अस्, आ, अम्, confused, confounded, disturbed in mind; (अस्), m. the moon; a species of camphor; killing, slaughter; (आ), f. hurting, injuring, injury; turmeric; cotton; a species of tree resembling the vine-palm; a switch; (अम्), n. strength, power.
पिञ्जट: पिञ्जट, अस्, m. the concrete rheum of the eyes.
पिञ्जन: पिञ्जन, अम्, n. a bow or bow-shaped instrument used for cleaning cotton.
पिञ्जर: पिञ्जर, अस्, आ, अम्, reddish-yellow, yellow or tawny, of the colour of gold; (अस्), m. tawny-brown or reddish-yellow colour, a mixture of red and yellow; a horse (probably a bay or chesnut); N. of a mountain; (अम्), n. gold; yellow orpiment; the flower of Mesua Roxburghii; a cage; the ribs or the cavity formed by them, the thorax; a skeleton; [cf. पञ्जर।] —पिञ्जर-ता, f. yellowish-red (the colour).
पिञ्जरक: पिञ्जरक, अस्, m., N. of a Nāga; (अम्), n. orpiment.
पिञ्जरित: पिञ्जरित, अस्, आ, अम्, coloured reddish-yellow.
पिञ्जल: पिञ्जल, अस्, आ, अम्, extremely perplexed or con-founded, disturbed, overcome with terror or grief; panic-struck, being in great disorder; (आ), f., N. of a river; (ई), f. two blades of Kuśa grass serving as an implement to hold certain articles at a sacrifice; (अम्), n. the leaf of the Kuśa grass; the plant Cur-cuma Zerumbet (हरिद्राभ); yellow orpiment.
पिञ्जलक: पिञ्जलक, अस्, आ, अम्, in उत्-पिञ्जलक, extremely confounded or disturbed, being in great disorder.
पिञ्जिका: पिञ्जिका, f. a roll of cotton from which threads are spun.
पिञ्जूल: पिञ्जूल, अम्, n., Ved. a bundle of stalks, a bundle of grass, &c.; the wick of a lamp; (sometimes spelt पिञ्जुल।)
पिञ्जूलक: पिञ्जूलक, अस्, m., N. of a man; (आस्), m. pl., N. of his descendants.
पिञ्जूष: पिञ्जूष, अस्, m. the wax of the ear (= पेञ्जूष).
पिञ्जेट: पिञ्जेट, अस्, m. the excretion or concrete rheum of the eyes; [cf. पिञ्जट।]
पिञ्जोला: पिञ्जोला पिञ्जोला, f. the noise or rustling of leaves.
पिट्: पिट् पिट्, cl. 1. P. पेटति, पेटितुम्, to sound; to assemble or heap together.
पिट: पिट, अस्, m. a basket for holding grain, a sort of cupboard or granary made of bamboos or canes; a basket, box; (अम्), n. a house, a hovel; a roof.
पिटक: पिटक, अस्, आ, अम्, m. f. n. (usually n.), a basket, box; a large basket or receptacle of basket-work for keeping grain &c., a granary; a collection of writings [cf. त्रि-प्°]; a boil, blister, ulcer; a kind of orna-ment on Indra's banner; (अस्), m., N. of a man.
पिटक्या: पिटक्या, f. a multitude of baskets.
पिटाक: पिटाक, see Gaṇa to Pāṇ. IV. 2, 49; (अस्), m., N. of a man; N. of a sage.
पिटङ्काकी: पिटङ्काकी पिटङ्काकी or पिटङ्कोकी, f. the plant Cucumis Colocynthis.
पिटङ्काश: पिटङ्काश पिटङ्काश, अस्, m. a kind of fish, a species of pike, Esax Scolopax, Silurus Pabda.
पिट्टक: पिट्टक पिट्टक, अम्, n. the tartar or excre-tion of the teeth; [cf. किट्ट, किट्टक, पिप्पिका।]
पिट्टय: पिट्टय पिट्टय (fr. पिट्ट = पिष्ट?), Nom. P. पिट्टयति, -यितुम्, Ved. to stamp or press into a solid mass.
पिट्टित: पिट्टित, अस्, आ, अम्, stamped into a solid mass, pressed flat.
पिठ्: पिठ् पिठ्, cl. 1. P. पेठति, पेठितुम्, to injure, hurt, kill; to feel pain or affliction.
पिठर: पिठर, अस्, ई, अम्, m. f. n. a pot, pan; (अस्), m. an addition to a building shaped like a hollow vessel, a hut made of bamboos and mats, or accord-ing to some a kind of store-room or scullery; N. of a particular Agni; N. of a Dānava; (अम्), n. a churning-stick; the root of Cyperus Rotundus.
पिठरक: पिठरक, अस्, m. (?), a pot, pan; N. of a Nāga. —पिठरक-कपाल, अस्, अम्, m. n. a fragment of a pot, potsherd.
पिठीनस्: पिठीनस् पिठीनस्, आस्, m., N. of a man.
पिडक: पिडक पिडक, अस्, m. or पिडका, f. a small boil, pimple, papula, pustule. —पिडका-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, having boils, pimples, &c.
पिडकिन्: पिडकिन्, ई, इनी, इ, having boils, &c.
पिण्ड्: पिण्ड् पिण्ड् (probably akin to rt. पिष्; considered by some as a Nom. fr. पिण्ड below), cl. 1. A., 10. P. पिण्डते, पिण्डितुम्, पिण्-डयति, -यितुम्, to roll into a lump or ball, to put together, join, unite; to accumulate; to assemble.
पिण्ड: पिण्ड, अस्, अम्, m. n. (in most senses usually m.), a round mass, ball, globe, lump, knob, clod (e. g. अयः-पिण्ड, a ball or lump of iron; अग्नि-पिण्डौ, the knobs at the end of a pair of tongs; cf. नेत्र-प्°, मृत्-प्°); a roundish lump of food, a bite, morsel, mouthful; a cake or ball of meal offered to the Manes, a ball or lump of meat or rice mixed up with milk, curds, flowers, &c., and offered at the several Śrāddhas to the Manes by the nearest surviving relations (= नि-वाप); food; sustenance, means of living, livelihood, subsistence [cf. पर-पिण्डाद]; alms; flesh, meat; the embryo or fetus in an early stage of gestation; the body; the projection of an elephant's frontal sinus; a round button; anything roundish, thick, gross, or solid; thickness (one of the three dimensions in geometry); a heap, cluster, quantity, collection; an object; a particular part of a house; a sort of portico or shed in front of the door; myrrh, incense, frankincense; the side imme-diately below the armpit (?); Vangueria Spinosa; the flower of the China rose; (in arithmetic) sum, total amount; (in astronomy) a sine expressed in numbers [cf. ज्या-प्°]; the twenty-fourth part of the quadrant of a circle, or 3° 45; N. of a man; (औ), m. du. the fleshy parts of the shoulder situated above the collar-bone; (अम्), n. power, might; an army; iron; fresh butter; (ई), f. a round mass, &c. (= पिण्ड, m.); a long gourd, Cucurbita Lagenaria (= अ-लाबु); a species of date tree; the flowering shrub Tabernæ-montana Coronaria (= तगर); the plant Jonesia Aśoka; a species of palm, Phœnix Dactylifera; पिण्डत्वं गम्, to attain the condition of a lump. —पिण्ड-द, अस्, आ, अम्, giving or qualified to give the funeral cake to deceased ancestors; supplying with bread or with the means of subsistence; (अस्), m. the nearest male relation who offers the funeral cake; a patron, master. —पिण्ड-दातृ, ता, त्री, तृ, one who gives or is qualified to give the funeral cake to deceased ancestors. —पिण्ड-दान, अम्, n. offering a cake of meal (especially in the oblation to the Manes); presentation of the obsequial cake; the funeral oblation made to deceased ancestors on the evening of new moon. —पिण्ड-निर्वपण, अम्, n. presenting obsequial cakes to the Manes, the sacrifice to the Manes. —पिण्ड-पद, अम्, n. a kind of arithmetical calculation. —पिण्ड-पात, अस्, m. giving alms. —पिण्डपातिक, अस्, m. one who lives on alms. —पिण्ड-पात्र, अम्, n. the vessel in which the obsequial cakes are offered to the Manes; alms (lit. an alms-dish). —पिण्ड-पाद or पिण्ड-पाद्य, अस्, m. ‘thick-footed,’ an elephant. —पिण्ड-पितृ-यज्ञ, अम्, n., Ved. the oblation of obsequial cakes to deceased ancestors on the evening of new moon. —पिण्ड-पुष्प, अस्, m. the tree Jonesia Aśoka; the China rose; the pomegranate tree; (अम्), n. the blossom of the Aśoka tree; the flower of the China rose; a lotus; the flower of the plant Tabernæmontana Coronaria. —पिण्डपुष्पक, अस्, m. a kind of vegetable, Chenopodium Album. —पिण्ड-फल, अस्, आ, अम्, bearing (long) round fruits; (आ), f. a bitter gourd. —पिण्ड-बीज or पिण्ड-वीज, अस्, m. a flowering shrub, Nerium (or Oleander) Odorum. —पिण्डबीजक, अस्, m. Pterospermum Acerifolium (= कर्णिकार). —पिण्ड-भाज्, क्, क्, क्, partaking of a funeral oblation, entitled to a share in the funeral cake, eating or receiving the cakes offered at a funeral ceremony; (जस्), m. pl. de-ceased ancestors, the Manes. —पिण्ड-भृति, इस्, f. means of subsistence, livelihood. —पिण्ड-मय, अस्, ई, अम्, consisting of a lump (of clay). —पिण्ड-मात्रोपजीविन् (°र-उप्°), ई, इनी, इ, subsisting on a mere morsel. —पिण्ड-मुस्ता, f. a species of grass, Cyperus Pertenuis. —पिण्ड-मूल or पिण्ड-मू-लक, अम्, n. a carrot, Daucus Carota (= गर्जर)। —पिण्ड-यज्ञ, अस्, m. the oblation of obsequial cakes to deceased ancestors. —पिण्ड-लेप, अस्, m. the particles or fragments of the obsequial cakes which cling to the hands, (these are offered to the three ancestors preceding the great-grandfather.) —पिण्ड-लोप, अस्, m. an interruption in offering the funeral cake; a neglect of the solemn obsequies in honour of deceased ancestors. —पिण्ड-वत्, ind. like a lump or ball. —पिण्ड-सम्बन्ध, अस्, m. relationship between a living person and one deceased sufficiently near to qualify the former to offer the obsequial cake to the latter; [cf. स-पिण्ड।] —पिण्ड-सम्बन्धिन्, ई, इनी, इ, qualified by near relationship to a living person to receive the obsequial cake from him at the oblation to the Manes. —पिण्ड-सेक्तृ, ता, m., N. of a Nāga. —पिण्ड-स्थ, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. ‘mingled in a lump,’ mixed or intermingled together. —पिण्डान्वाहार्य (°ड-अन्°), अस्, आ, अम्, to be eaten after the funeral cake has been offered (Manu III. 123). —पिण्डान्वाहार्यक, अम्, n. (with श्राद्ध) a meal in honour of the Manes after offering the funeral cakes. —पिण्डाभ्र (°ड-अभ्°), अम्, n. hail. —पिण्डायस (°ड-अय्°), अम्, n. steel. —पिण्डालु (°ड-आलु), उस्, m., N. of two bulbous plants; = कन्द-गुडूची; an esculent medicinal root described as sweet, cooling, and diuretic (= Hindī peḍālu Bengālī cuvaḍiālu; in this sense also पिण्डालुक, अम्, n.). —पिण्डाश or पिण्डाशक (°ड-आश्°), or पिण्डाशन (°ड-अश्°), अस्, or पिण्डाशिन् (°ड-आश्°), ई, m. ‘eating morsels,’ a beg-gar. —पिण्डाह्वा (°ड-आह्°), f. the resin of Gardenia Gummifera (= नाडी-हिङ्गु). —पिण्डी-खण्ड, अस्, or अम्, m. or n. (?), a small wood of Tabernæmontana Coronaria trees (or of Aśoka trees). —पिण्डी-जङ्घ, अस्, m., N. of a man or of his descendants. —पिण्डी-तगर, अस्, m. a species of Tabernæmontana Coro-naria (= कफ-वर्धन). —पिण्डीतगरक, अस्, m. Tabernæmontana Coronaria. —पिण्डी-तरु, उस्, m. a species of tree (= महा-प्°). —पिण्डी-पुष्प, अम्, n. Jonesia Aśoka. —पिण्डी-लेप, अस्, m. a kind of unguent. —पिण्डी-शूर, अस्, m. ‘a cake-hero,’ a cowardly boaster, cotquean, braggart. —पिण्डोदक-क्रिया (°ड-उद्°), f. an oblation of obsequial cakes and water. —पिण्डोद्धरण (°ड-उद्°), अम्, n. participating in funeral offerings, presenting them to common ancestors. —पिण्डोपनिषद् (°ड-उप्°), त्, f., N. of an Upaniṣad.
पिण्डक: पिण्डक, अस्, अम्, m. n. a lump, lump of food; a round swelling or protuberance [cf. मस्तक-प्°]; the calf of the leg; incense, myrrh; a species of bulbous plant (= पिण्डालु); a carrot, Daucus Carota; (in astronomy) a sine expressed in numbers; (अस्), m. a Piśāca, goblin, demon; (इका), f. a globular swelling or protuberance, a fleshy swelling (in the shoulders, arms, legs, &c.), a wen (?); the calf of the leg; the instep; the nave of a wheel; a stool or seat of various shapes and dimensions; a base or pedestal for the image of a deity or for a Liṅga (Ved.); a kind of shrub (= श्वेताम्लि).
पिण्डन: पिण्डन, अम्, n. forming globes, taking a globular form (as water); (अस्), m. a mound or bank.
पिण्डरक: पिण्डरक, अस् or अम्, m. or n. (?), a bridge.
पिण्डल: पिण्डल, अस्, m. a bridge, causeway, passage over a stream or ravine, a mound, ridge, balk raised to form a path across inundated fields; [cf. पिण्डन, पिण्डिल।]
पिण्डस: पिण्डस, अस्, m. a beggar, mendicant living upon alms; [cf. पिण्डाश under पिण्ड।]
पिण्डार: पिण्डार, अस्, m. a beggar, religious mendicant; a buffalo-herdsman, neatherd, cowherd; a species of tree, Flacourtia Sapida; Trewia Nudiflora; an expression of censure; N. of a Nāga; (अम्), n. a kind of vegetable (= Hindī पिण्डारा).
पिण्डारक: पिण्डारक, अस्, m., N. of a Nāga; N. of a Vṛṣṇi; of a son of Vasu-deva and Rohiṇī; of a river considered holy by the Hindūs; (अम्), n., N. of a place of pilgrimage in Guzerat. —पिण्डारक-तीर्थ, अम्, n., N. of a sacred bathing-place.
पिण्डि: पिण्डि, इस्, f. the nave of a wheel (= पिण्डी, पिण्डिका).
पिण्डिक: पिण्डिक, अस्, आ, अम्, having large calves (?). See पिण्डिका under पिण्डक, col. 2.
पिण्डित: पिण्डित, अस्, आ, अम्, rolled into a ball or lump, pressed into a solid mass; thick, massy, lumpish; formed into a mass, heaped together, collected; mixed, intermingled with; united; added, multiplied; counted, numbered; (अस्), m. incense.
पिण्डिन्: पिण्डिन्, ई, इनी, इ, possessing a body (= शरीरिन्); receiving cakes of meal (as ancestors &c.); possessing the पिण्ड or funeral oblation; (ई), m. a beggar; an offerer of obsequial oblations or cakes of meal to the Manes.
पिण्डिल: पिण्डिल, अस्, आ, अम्, having large calves (= स्थूल-जङ्घ); skilled in calculations; (अस्), m. a skilful calculator or arithmetician, a calculator of nati-vities, astrologer, astronomer; a bridge, mound, balk, causeway; (आ), f. a species of cucumber, Cucumis Maderaspatanus (= गोडुम्बा).
पिण्डीकृ: पिण्डी-कृ, cl. 8. P. A. -करोति, -कुरुते, -कर्-तुम्, to make into a lump or ball, press together, unite, join together, mix or intermingle; to con-centrate; to identify with (with सह). —पिण्डी-क-रण, अम्, n. making into a lump or ball, heaping. —पिण्डी-कृत, अस्, आ, अम्, made into a lump or ball. —पिण्डी-कृत्य, ind. having made into a lump or ball; having concentrated.
पिण्डीतक: पिण्डीतक, अस्, m. the tree Vangueria Spinosa; a kind of shrub, Tabernæmontana Coronaria; a species of basil (= फणिज्झक); (अम्), n. the fruit of the tree Vangueria Spinosa.
पिण्डीभू: पिण्डी-भू, cl. 1. P. -भवति, -भवितुम्, to be made into a lump or ball, to become a solid body. —पिण्डी-भाव, अस्, m. the being rolled together into a ball. —पिण्डी-भूत, अस्, आ, अम्, formed into a lump or ball, lumped, heaped.
पिण्डीर: पिण्डीर, अस्, आ, अम्, sapless, juiceless, arid, dry; (अस्), m. the pomegranate tree [cf. कृष्ण-प्°]; cuttle-fish bone; sea foam.
पिण्डोल: पिण्डोल, अस्, m., N. of a man.
पिण्डोलि: पिण्डोलि, इस्, f. leavings of a meal, fragments dropped from the mouth, orts.
पिण्डिपाल: पिण्डिपाल पिण्डिपाल, अस् or अम्, m. or n. (?), N. of a weapon with a single point; [cf. भिन्दि-पाल।]
पिण्या: पिण्या पिण्या, f. heart-pea, Cardiosper-mum Halicacabum (= पण्या).
पिण्याक: पिण्याक पिण्याक, अस्, अम्, m. n. (said to be fr. rt. पिष्), the residue of seeds which have been ground for oil; oil-cake; incense; saffron; Asa Fœtida; (आ), f. a species of plant.
पितु: पितु पितु, उस्, m., Ved. (fr. rt. प्यै), juice, drink; nourishment; (Sāy.) = पालकम् अन्-नम्, nourishing food. —पितु-कृत्, त्, त्, त्, Ved. bestowing or providing food. —पितु-भाज्, क्, क्, क्, Ved. enjoying or partaking of food; (Sāy.) = अन्-नार्थिन्, seeking or earning food. —पितु-भृत्, त्, त्, त्, Ved. bringing food. —पितु-मत्, आन्, अती, अत्, Ved. accompanied by food, abounding in food, nou-rishing. —पितु-षणि, इस्, इस्, इ, Ved. bestowing or granting food. —पितु-स्तोम, अस्, m. ‘praise of food,’ N. of the hymn Ṛg-veda I. 187.
पितूय: पितूय, Nom. P. पितूयति, -यितुम्, Ved. to long for food, desire food.
पितृ: पितृ पितृ, ता, m. (fr. rt. 3. पा), a father; (in the Veda पितृ is an epithet of Bṛhas-pati, Varuṇa, Prajā-pati, and especially of heaven or the sky; अन्तरा पितरम् मातरञ्-च, between heaven and earth; according to Sāy. पितृ = पालक, a protector); (तरौ), m. du. father and mother, parents, (in the Veda an epithet of the Araṇis or two pieces of wood regarded as the parents of Fire, and of heaven and earth regarded as the parents of all beings); (तरस्), m. pl. fathers, forefathers, ancestors; a father and his brothers, father and uncles, paternal ancestors; the spirits of departed an-cestors, the Manes or spirits of the dead (they are of two kinds, viz. either the spirits of the father, grand-fathers, and great-grandfathers of an individual or the progenitors of mankind generally, to both classes of whom Śrāddhas or obsequial worship is paid and oblations of food called Piṇḍas presented; they in-habit a peculiar region, which, according to some, is the Bhuvas or region of the air, according to others, the orbit of the moon, and are considered as the regents of the Nakṣatras Maghā and Mūla); [cf. Zend pita, base pa-tar: Gr. πα-τήρ, πάτρω-ς: Lat. pa-ter, Jup-piter: Goth. fa-dar: Old Germ. fa-tar, fa-ter, ‘father;’ fataro, ‘uncle:’ Angl. Sax. faeder, ‘father;’ fadhu, ‘aunt, father's sister:’ Hib. athair, ‘father,’ for pathair.], —पितरि-शूर, अस्, m. ‘a hero against his father,’ a cowardly boaster. —पिता-पुत्र, औ, m. du. father and son. —पितापुत्र-विरोध, अस्, m. a contest between father and son. —पितापुत्र-समागम, अस्, m., N. of a Buddhist Sūtra. —पितापुत्रीय, अस्, आ, अम्, relating to father and son; containing the words पितृ and पुत्र; (with सम्प्रदान) the transmission (of bodily capacities and powers) from father to son. —पिता-मह, अस्, m. a paternal grandfather; a N. of Brahmā the great father of all; N. of the author of a Dharma-śāstra; of the author of an astronomical work; (आस्), m. pl. the ancestors, Manes; (ई), f. a paternal grandmother. —पितामह-सरस्, अस्, n. or पितामहस्य सरस्, N. of a place of pilgrimage. —पिता-सुमति-संवाद, अस्, m., N. of a part of the Brahma-vaivarta-Purāṇa. —पितुः-पुत्र, अस्, m. a father's son. —पितुः-ष्वसृ or पितुः-स्वसृ, सा, f. a father's sister. —पितृ-कर्मन्, अ, or पितृ-कार्य, अम्, n. obsequial rites, sacrifice offered to deceased ancestors. —पितृ-कल्प, अस्, m. (perhaps) legends relating to ancestors; N. of a long period of time, Brahmā's day of new moon. —पितृ-कानन, अम्, n. ‘grove of ancestors,’ a cemetery. —पितृ-कुल्या, f. ‘rivulet of the Pitṛs,’ N. of a river rising in the Malaya mountains. —पितृ-कृत, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. committed against parents or an-cestors (as sin). —पितृ-कृत्य, अम्, n. or पितृ-क्रिया, f. obsequial rites, oblations offered to the spirits of deceased ancestors. —पितृ-गण, अस्, m. the whole body of ancestors collectively, a group or class of Manes or deceased progenitors who were sons of the Ṛṣis or Prajā-patis, (the principal classes, according to Manu III. 194-199, are the Soma-sads, descended from Vi-rāj, the Agni-ṣvāttas from Marīci, Barhi-shads from Atri, Soma-pās from Bhṛgu, Haviṣ-mats from Aṅgiras, Ājya-pas from Pulastya, and Su-kālins from Vasiṣṭha; there are also the Agni-dagdhas and An-agnidagdhas, Kāvyas and Saumyas.) —पितृ-गणा, f. an epithet of Durgā. —पितृ-गाथा, आस्, f. pl. ‘songs of the ancestors,’ an epithet of particular songs. —पितृ-गामिन्, ई, इनी, इ, be-longing or pertaining to a father. —पितृ-गृणा, f. probably a wrong reading for पितृ-गणा, q. v. —पितृ-गृह, अम्, n. a father's house, paternal mansion; ‘house of ancestors,’ a burial ground, ceme-tery. —पितृ-ग्रह, अस्, m. ‘the genius of the Manes,’ N. of a demon causing disease. —पितृ-घातक, अस्, or पितृ-घातिन्, ई, m. ‘slaying a father,’ a parricide. —पितृ-चेट, अस्, m., N. of a man. —पितृ-तम, अस्, m., Ved., in पितृतमः पित्रीणां, best of the ancestors (Sāy. = पाल-कानाम् मध्ये अतिशयेन पालकः, a defender in the highest degree among defenders). —पितृ-तर्-पण, अम्, n. ‘refreshing the Manes,’ gifts in honour of deceased progenitors, distributed at the Śrāddhas or funeral ceremonies; an oblation to the Manes; the act of throwing water out of the right hand at seasons of ablution as an offering to the Manes or deceased ancestors in general; the part of the hand between the thumb and fore-finger sacred to the Manes; sesamum (= तिल). —पितृ-तस्, ind., Ved. from the father, on the father's side. —पितृ-तिथि, इस्, f. day of new moon, a day sacred to the Manes of either deceased parent, the day appointed for obsequial rites to deceased ancestors. —पितृ-तीर्थ, अम्, n. ‘the place of pilgrimage for proge-nitors,’ epithet of the city called Gayā (where the performance of funeral sacrifices is peculiarly meri-torious and efficacious); the part of the hand be-tween the fore-finger and thumb sacred to the Manes. —पितृतीर्थ-माहात्म्य, अम्, n., N. of a chapter of the Śiva-Purāṇa. —पितृ-त्व, अम्, n. fatherhood, paternity; the state or condition of a Pitṛ or deified progenitor. —पितृ-दत्त, अस्, आ, अम्, given by a father (a term applied to a woman's peculiar property); (अस्), m., N. of a man. —पितृ-दयिता, f., N. of a work. —पितृ-दान or पितृ-दानक, अम्, n. a gift in honour of deceased an-cestors, an offering to the Manes. —पितृ-दाय, अस्, m. property inherited from a father, patrimony. —पितृ-देव, आस्, m. pl. the Manes and the gods; the divine Manes; (अस्, आ, अम्), worshipping a father; relating to the worship of the Manes or deceased ancestors. —पितृ-देवत or पितृ-देवत्य, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. having the Manes for deities, sacred to the Manes. —पितृ-दैवत, अस्, ई, अम्, relating to the worship of the Manes; governed or presided over by the Manes; (अम्), n. epithet of the tenth lunar asterism or Maghā. —पितृ-दैवत्य, अस्, आ, अम्, relating to the worship of the Manes; (अम्), n., N. of a sacrifice offered to the Manes on the day called Aṣṭakā. —पितृ-द्रव्य, अम्, n. ‘father's substance,’ patrimony. —पितृ-नामन्, आ, म्नी, अ, called after the father's name; [cf. मातृ-नामन्।] —पितृ-पक्ष, अस्, m. paternal side, paternal relationship; the half month of the Manes, N. of the dark half in the Gauṇa Āśvina, so termed as peculiarly appointed for the celebration of obse-quial rites to the Pitṛs or Manes; a father's relations, relatives by the father's side; (अस्, आ, अम्), being on the father's side. —पितृ-पति, इस्, m. ‘lord of the Manes,’ an epithet of Yama, regent of the dead; (अयस्), m. pl. the Manes and the lords of creatures (Prajā-patis). —पितृ-पद, अम्, n. the world or state of the Manes. —पितृ-पात्र, अम्, n. a cup or other vessel used at obsequial rites. —पितृ-पितृ, ता, m. a father's father, paternal grandfather. —पितृ-पीत, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. drunk by ancestors or deceased progenitors. —पितृ-पूजन, अम्, n. worship of the Manes. —पितृ-पैतामह, अस्, ई, अम्, inherited or derived from father and grandfather; (आस्), m. pl. fathers and grandfathers, ancestors. —पितृपैता-महिक, अस्, ई, अम्, inherited or derived from father and grandfather. —पितृ-प्रसू, ऊस्, f. a father's mother; ‘mother of the Manes,’ twilight (the time when the Manes of departed ancestors are abroad). —पितृ-प्राप्त, अस्, आ, अम्, received from a father; inherited patrimonially. —पितृ-प्रिय, अस्, m. ‘dear to the Pitṛs,’ a species of plant (= भृङ्ग-राज). —पितृ-बन्धु, उस्, m. a kinsman by the father's side, as the son of the paternal grandfather's sister, of the paternal grandmother's sister, and of the father's maternal uncle; (उ), n. relationship by the father's side. —पितृ-बान्धव, अस्, m. a kins-man in the paternal line. —पितृ-भक्त, अस्, आ, अम्, dutifully attached to a father. —पितृ-भक्ति, इस्, f. filial duty to a father. —पितृभक्ति-तरङ्-गिणी, f., N. of a work. —पितृ-भूति, इस्, m., N. of a commentator on Kātyāyana's Śrauta-sūtras. —पितृ-भोजन, अम्, n. a father's food; food offered to the Manes; (अस्, अम्), m. n. the plant Phaseolus Radi-atus (a species of pulse = माष). —पितृ-भ्रातृ, ता, m. a father's brother, paternal uncle. —पितृ-मत्, आन्, अती, अत्, having a father, having an illus-trious father; accompanied by the Manes, connected with the Manes (as Soma or Yama); mentioning the Manes or deceased ancestors. —पितृ-मन्दिर, अम्, n. a father's house, paternal mansion; ‘dwelling-place of ancestors,’ a cemetery. —पितृ-मातृ-हीन, अस्, आ, अम्, destitute of father and mother, orphan. —पितृ-मेध or पितृ-यज्ञ, अस्, m. sacrifice offered to the Manes, obsequial offerings. —पितृ-याण, Ved. or पितृ-यान, अस्, आ, अम्, trodden by the Manes;
